limits: Full language services, types, typed reference expansion, parameter types and confirmed join suggestions require T116-T119; no local replacement resolver was added.
Partial semantic index acceptance remains pending the new analyzer contract.
Full-text validation is structural; identifiers, types and full query semantics require analyzer/platform validation.

The platform rejected DISTINCT + AUTOORDER without the required ordering fields in the projection. ESKA does not infer those fields; the final positive modifier case verifies ALLOWED/TOP/FOR UPDATE/AUTOORDER, while DISTINCT is covered separately.
At most one executable totals section; DROP is used for temporary-table deletion.
Windows, macOS, VS Code and Remote remain unverified.
Benchmark series use one profile per variant; memory values are process/target samples, not whole-system usage or proof of absence of long-term leaks.

diagnosticAttempts.explanation: Earlier XML tests relied on native dirty-close decisions, saved a source after workspace/open, or compared a BOM-bearing disk file directly to the native buffer. The final fixture is prepared before workspace/open; XML Save is tested as a separate explicit operation after constructor application. New form/table selectors were also adapted. No source safety checks were weakened.
diagnosticAttempts.platform: Initial UNION move expectation read the named N column incorrectly; corrected expected values. DISTINCT/AUTOORDER failure retained as semantic evidence; PostgreSQL was initially stopped, then started only for the owned repeat and restored to exited state.
